findings.title: All-groups VIEW permission grants realm-wide group manage
findings.body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() returns true when hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE) succeeds, so an admin who only has the Groups VIEW scope on the all-groups resource is treated as allowed to manage every group. requireManage() is the gate for creating top-level groups (GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup) and other mutations that call canManage() with no group. A view-only fine-grained permission therefore authorizes group creation and other manage operations. canManage() must require MANAGE (or MANAGE_USERS), not VIEW.

findings.title: Group member search uses authorization resource ids, not group ids
findings.body: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() walks resources with findByType and then calls hasPermission(groupResource.getId()) and granted.add(groupResource.getId()). In the V2 schema the group id is the resource name (resolveGroup returns group.getId(), and getOrCreateResource stores that as the name); getId() is the authorization resource UUID. hasPermission looks that UUID up with findByName, misses the group resource, and either skips the permission or falls back to the all-groups resource. The set stored on the session as UserModel.GROUPS (UsersResource and BruteForceUsersResource searches, and getUsersCount) therefore does not contain group ids. Admins granted view-members or manage-members on specific groups get empty user searches and zero counts, or a filter on ids that match no groups.

findings.title: Per-group authorization resources are created without the Groups type
findings.body: getOrCreateResource creates a resource named with the group id and updates scopes, but never calls setType(GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE). Only the schema all-groups resource created in init() has type Groups. GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() discovers candidates solely via resourceStore.findByType(..., GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE). Individual group resources are invisible to that scan, so view-members and manage-members permissions on a single group never contribute group ids to user search or user counts. V1 set the type explicitly ("Group"); V2 needs the same when creating the resource.

findings.title: Existing admin-permissions clients never gain Groups scopes or resources
findings.body: init() returns immediately when realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() is already set, and this change only adds Groups (and manage-membership, manage-members, view-members) to the schema used at first creation. Realms that already enabled fine-grained admin permissions V2 keep a client with no Groups resource type and no new scopes. Creating a group permission then hits getOrCreateResource, which throws ModelException("No scopes found.") when scopeStore.findByName cannot resolve the new scope names. Permission checks that fall back to getResourceTypeResource also get null and then NPE in GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission on policyStore.findByResource(server, null) or resource.getScopes(). Enabling the feature must migrate an existing admin-permissions client, not only bootstrap a new one.

findings.title: Group permission resources have no display name
findings.body: getResourceName() only special-cases the Users resource type and otherwise returns resource.getDisplayName(). Group resources are created with the group id as the name and no display name, and this PR never teaches getResourceName to resolve GROUPS the way it resolves users to usernames. Admin APIs and the UI that list fine-grained permissions will show a null name for every group resource instead of the group name or path.

findings.title: requireManageMembers javadoc cites the wrong check
findings.body: The new javadoc on requireManageMembers says it throws if canManageMembership(GroupModel) returns false. The method is required to enforce canManageMembers. Callers and implementors following the comment will apply the membership scope instead of manage-members.
